title: Summit Earning Basis of Each Crestline Fare Brand
content:
**Earning chart — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** When a coupon is flown it passes to the passenger's Summit membership for accrual on the earning basis of the fare brand. The fare brand sets two figures; the per-dollar earning rates themselves belong to the loyalty program.

| Fare brand | Qualifying dollars, percent of the segment fare | Cabin bonus, percent of the base award miles |
|---|---|---|
| Crestline Basic Economy | 50 | 0 |
| Crestline Main Cabin | 100 | 0 |
| Crestline Main Plus | 100 | 0 |
| Crestline Main Flexible | 100 | 0 |
| Crestline Premium Economy | 100 | 25 |
| Crestline First | 100 | 50 |

- **Qualifying dollars**: the share of the segment fare counted as Summit qualifying dollars when the coupon is flown.
- **Cabin bonus**: bonus award miles on a flown coupon of the brand, as a percent of the base award miles.

*Hypothetical illustration.* A flown Crestline Basic Economy segment with a 180-dollar segment fare counts 90 qualifying dollars (50 percent of 180); the same fare on Crestline Main Cabin counts 180. A Crestline First coupon that earns 2,000 base award miles adds a cabin bonus of 1,000 miles (50 percent of 2,000).
